seo.heading: Free 3D Cargo Loading Optimizer
seo.intro: LDMCalculator helps logistics teams plan how cargo, pallets and boxes fit into trucks, containers, planes and ships. Visualize the load in 3D, find the optimal stacking pattern and reduce wasted space and trips.
seo.how1: Pick the vehicle type and trailer or container size that matches your shipment.
seo.how2: Enter every product's length, width, height, weight, quantity and stackability — or switch to total tonnage mode for a single SKU.
seo.how3: Get an instant 3D plan with loading meters (LDM), volume efficiency and a per-item breakdown you can screenshot and share.
seo.whyBody: Built for shippers, freight forwarders and 3PLs. The 3D bin-packing engine accounts for stacking limits, rotation, weight distribution and trailer length so you stop guessing and start filling vehicles to their real capacity. No signup, no install, works in any modern browser.

faq.q: What is LDM (loading meter) and how is it calculated?
faq.a: Loading meter (LDM) represents one full meter of trailer length used at full width and stackable height. LDMCalculator computes it from the longest used position along your trailer divided by 100 cm — so 6.80m of cargo across a 13.60m trailer is 6.80 LDM.

faq.q: How does the 3D bin-packing algorithm choose a layout?
faq.a: It places larger and heavier items first, tries each rotation you allow, and fills gaps using a greedy guillotine strategy. Stack height is capped per SKU and total trailer weight is enforced.

faq.q: Can I optimize loading by total tonnage instead of unit count?
faq.a: Yes. On the product step, enable "Calculate by total tonnage" and enter the unit weight plus the total tons. The system derives quantity automatically and reports how many tons fit and how many are left over.

faq.q: Does it consider weight distribution across the axles?
faq.a: Yes. Heavy SKUs are placed lower and toward the front of the trailer, and the engine refuses to exceed the maximum payload of the selected trailer or container.

faq.q: Which trailers and containers are supported?
faq.a: Standard and Mega tilt trailers, closed box trailers, custom-sized trailers, 20ft / 40ft / 40HC sea containers, rail containers and the most common air ULDs (PMC/PLA and high cube).
Yes — the core 3D loading calculator is free for unlimited use directly in your browser.

guide.title: How to complete a CMR
guide.intro: The CMR is the international consignment note for road freight. Fill it in before the goods are handed to the carrier — three signed copies travel with the shipment (sender, consignee, carrier).

s1.title: Sender & route
s1.desc: Enter the sender, consignee, the place/date the goods are taken over, the place of delivery and any attached documents.

s2.title: The goods
s2.desc: Per line, list marks & numbers, number of packages, packing method, nature of the goods, statistical number and gross/net weight.

s3.title: Instructions & payment
s3.desc: Add the sender’s instructions, how carriage is paid (Franco / Non Franco) and any cash-on-delivery amount.

s4.title: Carrier
s4.desc: The carrier fills the heavy-bordered boxes: carrier details, successive carriers, reservations, TIR carnet and plate number.

s5.title: Charges
s5.desc: Break down carriage charges, deductions, balance and supplementary costs, and state where the note was established.

s6.title: Signatures
s6.desc: Sender, carrier and consignee sign and stamp. The consignee signs box 24 on receipt of the goods.

guide.tip: Tip: use the zoom controls to enlarge the sheet, then click any field to type. “Print / PDF” produces a clean A4 sheet.

form.title: International Consignment Note
form.convention: This carriage is subject, notwithstanding any clause to the contrary, to the Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road (CMR).
form.f3: Place and date of taking over the goods (place, country)
form.f4: Place of delivery of the goods (place, country)
form.f14: Instructions as to payment for carriage
form.f22: Signature and stamp of the sender
form.f23: Signature and stamp of the carrier
form.f24: Signature and stamp of the consignee
form.demurrage: Damage caused by faulty loading, stowage or packing is the sender’s responsibility. Free time for loading/unloading is 48 hours; thereafter demurrage of EUR 200 per day applies.
form.vstripCarrier: Spaces with heavy borders must be filled in by the carrier.
form.vstripSender: To be completed under the sender’s responsibility.
form.vstripDanger: For dangerous goods, state the class, number and letter (if any) in the last line of columns 6–9.

guide.title: How to fill the invoice
guide.intro: This template is for export invoices with a Russian goods declaration. Enter party details, upload your logo and stamp, fill the line items and print.

s1.title: Parties
s1.desc: Enter the sender and recipient details in the boxes.

s2.title: Logo & stamp
s2.desc: Upload your logo and stamp; sign the signature area with mouse or touch.

s3.title: Invoice info
s3.desc: Enter invoice type, document no and the invoice / issue dates.

s4.title: Line items
s4.desc: On each row add the TN VED code, Russian goods name, quantity, unit price and total (EUR).

s5.title: Totals
s5.desc: Fill total quantity, discount, VAT and rate, then print or save as PDF.

guide.tip: Tip: use the zoom buttons to enlarge the form and click any field to type. “Print / PDF” produces a clean A4 page.
